status: draft for the owner's edit (slice (f) lane, 2026-09-06)
artist_scope: none (Tier 3: code-driven spinning rings; render-instance clones)
character_sheet: A drifting purple orb of three concentric rings, each ring six spokes, spinning on different axes at different speeds and shedding firework sparks. It floats through blocks, wanders to random points, sometimes homes on a target and hurts on contact, and the 'type 10' bomb form (the Queen's mad-mood cloud) explodes when it expires. It is an effect made into a creature: pure spin.
size_notes: 0.75 x 0.75 block hitbox; drawn at x1 for type 0, x0.55 for the other types (PurplePowerRenderer).

groups.name: rings
groups.phase: three fresh rolls of the level's random per RENDERED FRAME (nextFloat() * 360 degrees) — no rate, no period
groups.axis: x (the inner fan), y (the middle fan, under the carried X), z (the outer fan, under the carried X and Y)
groups.amplitude: any angle: a fresh random roll every frame
groups.plain: every frame each ring jumps to a fresh random angle: the inner fan about X, the middle fan about Y under the inner's X roll (applied twice), the outer fan about Z under both — a flicker, not a spin
groups.math: x = rand*360; Shape1__fan.xRot = rad(x); y = rand*360; Shape2__carry_x1.xRot = Shape2__carry_x2.xRot = rad(x); Shape2__fan.yRot = rad(y); z = rand*360; Shape3__carry_x1/x2.xRot = rad(x); Shape3__carry_y1/y2.yRot = rad(y); Shape3__fan.zRot = rad(z)

behaviour: Each ring is one classic part drawn six times at 60-degree steps (the __fan groups hold the roll; the __iN clones carry the static step) — Slice 4c's render-instance expansion; the carry groups repeat the earlier rolls the way the original's nested glRotatef calls did.

Every rendered frame re-rolls the three angles from the level's random (ENT-S-146, fixed 2026-09-06: the earlier port spun the rings at 7.3 / 5.1 / 3.7 degrees per tick, which the original never did); there is no period, no walk, no head.
texture_notes: Five canvases by type: purplepowertexture (type 0), 2, 3, 4 (types 1-3) and 10 (the bomb).
formulas: `PurplePowerGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations` (PurplePowerGeoReplacement.java:121-136) and the classic `ModelPurplePower.renderToBuffer` (ModelPurplePower.java:159-200; orig ModelPurplePower.java:44-86, `render`; ENT-S-146, fixed 2026-09-06): three rolls of the level's random per rendered frame, each `nextFloat() * 360` degrees — the first turns the inner fan about X (orig :57-58) and is carried as the middle and outer chains' X, applied twice (orig :58 and :64); the second turns the middle fan about Y (orig :66-67) and is carried as the outer chain's Y, twice (orig :67 and :73); the third turns the outer fan about Z (orig :75-76); each fan is one spoke drawn six times at 1.0471976-radian steps (orig :59-63 / :68-72 / :77-81). No input but the random is read: the walk, the age, the head and the attack flag play no part, and there is no period — every frame is a fresh roll.
